name: Molefolk
body:
These small, reclusive humanoids dwell in hidden subterranean caverns. They sometimes emerge at night to gather supplies, but they are rarely seen on the surface world during the day as they fear the harsh light of the sun.

Appearance

Molefolk bear a passing resemblance to moles and similar burrowing animals. They have wrinkled gray, pink, or alabaster skin that is quite durable, becoming so calloused in places as to resemble stone plating. This is covered by a fine layer of patchy fur that is usually gray but can also be black, brown, or green.

Their eyes are large and glow yellow in the dark, but they squint to narrow slits in bright light. Their snouts vary greatly-some having barely any nose at all, while others have great protruding starfish-shaped growths around their snouts to better sense vibrations while they burrow.

Their hands end in long, curved claws that work like shovels while they dig, but can also be used defensively. Their feet also end in short claws.

Molefolk dress in simple, conservative clothing woven out of fibers spun from insect silks and plant fibers grown in in their subterranean realms.

Social

To say that Subterranea is a dangerous place is an understatement, and molefolk have learned to protect themselves by remaining isolationist in the extreme. They use their superior burrowing abilities to find hidden caverns where they can barricade themselves away from their aggressive neighbors, predators, and natural hazards-only emerging when necessary to surreptitiously pillage what they cannot produce for themselves.

Molefolk society seems simplistic, even monotonous, by human standards. Most of a mole-person’s day is spent growing, preparing, and eating fungi and root vegetables, and maintaining the tribe’s farming and living spaces. They live by a simple code and simple beliefs that are passed down faithfully from generation to generation. Any spare time they may have is usually spent sitting in communal circles and discussing the crops or reaffirming the basic tenets of their cultural traditions.

Alignment and Religion

Molefolk have a strong leaning toward Lawful Neutral, with a tendency to blindly follow the practices established by countless generations before them. Challenging these traditions is anathema to them, and any deviation from this simple worldview is almost exclusively found among an explorer, adventurer, or diplomat who has had more experience with outsiders.

Molefolk traditionally practice a form of ancestor worship combined with ancient philosophical teachings. They are usually led by shamans, but clerics and druids are not uncommon, and there are also a fair number of molefolk who take levels in monk.

Names

Some typical names used by mole people include the following (choose or roll 1d12): 1 Atimaya, 2 Dankhala, 3 Eufazala, 4 Ishtirie, 5 Isofallawi, 6 Khavor, 7 Kherairn, 8 Makhar, 9 Mistarris, 10 Protomata, 11 Simbossat, 12 Solinduin

Common Traits
Ability Score Modifiers You are sturdy and quick, but slow to grasp new information. Your ability score modifiers are +2 Dex, +2 Con, -2 Int [specialized]. (1)
Size As a Small creature, you have a +1 size bonus on attack rolls, a +1 size bonus to your Armor Class, a -1 size penalty to your CMB, and a +4 size bonus on Stealth checks. You must use smaller weapons than Medium creatures. As a Small creature, you occupy a space of 5 feet by 5 feet. Your reach is 5 feet. (0)
Type You are a Monstrous Humanoid. (3)
Speed Your base speed is 20 feet. (-1)
Languages You begin play speaking Molespeak and Undercommon. If you have a high Intelligence score, you can choose from any of the following languages: Common, Dwarven, Gnome, and Terran. (0)
Other Traits
Burrow You have a burrow speed of 10 feet. (3)
Cave Dweller You gain a +1 bonus on Knowledge (dungeoneering) and Survival checks made underground. (1)
Claws While designed for digging, you can also use your two claws to make attacks. These are primary natural attacks that deal 1d3 damage each. (2)
Darkvision You have darkvision 120 feet. (1)
Light Blindness Abrupt exposure to bright light blinds you for 1 round; on subsequent rounds, you are dazzled as long as you remain in the affected area. (-2)
Natural Armor Your tough, resilient skin provides a +1 natural armor bonus to AC. (2)
Stability You gain a +4 species bonus to your CMD when resisting a bull rush or trip attempt while burrowing or standing on the ground. (1)
Total: 11 RP (advanced)
Alternate Traits
Beast Tamer Handle Animal is always a class skill for you. Once per day you can use speak with animals as a spell-like ability, using your character level as the caster level, but only to speak with burrowing or subterranean animals. This trait replaces cave dweller.
Climb Your claws are more adapted to climbing than burrowing. You have a climb speed of 20 feet, and gain the +8 species bonus on Climb checks that a climb speed normally grants. This trait replaces burrow.
Nomad You left your subterranean home behind to explore the world long ago. Your darkvision only extends to 60 feet, and you only have light sensitivity instead of light blindness. Knowledge (geography) and Survival are always class skills for you. This trait alters darkvision and replaces cave dweller and light blindness.
Subterranean Camouflage You gain a +4 species bonus to Stealth checks when in underground terrain. This trait replaces stability.
Tremorsense Your darkvision only extends to 60 feet, but you also have tremorsense with a range of 30 feet. This trait alters darkvision and replaces cave dweller.
Favored Class Bonuses
Barbarian Reduce the hardness of any object struck by your claws by 1/2 point (minimum 0).
Druid Add a +1 bonus on wild empathy checks made to influence animals and magical beasts that live underground.
Fighter Add +1 to your CMD when resisting a bull rush or trip maneuver.
Kineticist Add +1/3 point of damage to earth element blasts that deal damage.
Monk Add +1/4 point to your ki pool.
Ranger Add +1/2 foot to your burrow speed. In combat this option has no effect unless you have selected it ten times (5 feet) or another increment of ten.
Rogue Add a +1/2 bonus to your trap sense.
Shaman Add +1 spell from the cleric spell list that isn’t on the shaman spell list to your spell list for this class. This spell must be at least one spell level lower than the highest-level shaman spell you can cast.
Spiritualist Add +1 hit point to your phantom.

Awesome Ancestries: Fantasy Animal Humanoids, Vol. 3 - Born to Be Wild. © 2025, Far Distant Future Publishing; Author: Bryan Mangum.
